import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp

  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

end Hilbert.Deduction

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

instance [HasNecessitation H] : System.Necessitation H where
  nec := @λ φ d => rule (show { antecedents := [φ], consequence := □φ } ∈ H.rules by apply HasNecessitation.has_necessitation; simp_all) (by aesop);

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }

structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

  mdp := mdp

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end

  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

  mdp := mdp

  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α

  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

  nec := @λ φ d => rule (show { antecedents := [φ], consequence := □φ } ∈ H.rules by apply HasNecessitation.has_necessitation; simp_all) (by aesop);

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

instance [HasNecessitation H] : System.Necessitation H where
  nec := @λ φ d => rule (show { antecedents := [φ], consequence := □φ } ∈ H.rules by apply HasNecessitation.has_necessitation; simp_all) (by aesop);

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

instance [HasNecessitation H] : System.Necessitation H where
  nec := @λ φ d => rule (show { antecedents := [φ], consequence := □φ } ∈ H.rules by apply HasNecessitation.has_necessitation; simp_all) (by aesop);

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

  mdp := mdp

  imply₂ := imply₂

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

  mdp := mdp

  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end

  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

instance [HasNecessitation H] : System.Necessitation H where
  nec := @λ φ d => rule (show { antecedents := [φ], consequence := □φ } ∈ H.rules by apply HasNecessitation.has_necessitation; simp_all) (by aesop);

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by exact?

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by exact?

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by exact?

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by aesop

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where

instance : System.HasDiaDuality H := inferInstance

lemma maxm! {φ} (h : φ ∈ H.axioms) : H ⊢! φ := ⟨maxm h⟩

end Hilbert.Deduction


namespace Hilbert

open Deduction

class HasNecessitation (H : Hilbert α) where
  has_necessitation : ⟮Nec⟯ ⊆ H.rules := by exact?

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }

function, but the square brackets on the `[i : α]` argument means that it will

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

namespace Hilbert.Deduction

instance : System (Formula α) (Hilbert α) := ⟨Deduction⟩

instance : System.Lukasiewicz H where
  mdp := mdp
  imply₁ := imply₁
  imply₂ := imply₂
  elim_contra := ec

instance : System.Classical H where
annotation: instance : System.Classical H where

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _

  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

content_full:
import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)


variable {H H₁ H₂ : Hilbert α}

inductive Hilbert.Deduction (H : Hilbert α) : (Formula α) → Type _
  | maxm {φ}     : φ ∈ H.axioms → Deduction H φ
  | rule {rl}    : rl ∈ H.rules → (∀ {φ}, φ ∈ rl.antecedents → Deduction H φ) → Deduction H rl.consequence
  | mdp {φ ψ}    : Deduction H (φ ➝ ψ) → Deduction H φ → Deduction H ψ
  | imply₁ φ ψ   : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₁ φ ψ
  | imply₂ φ ψ χ : Deduction H $ Axioms.Imply₂ φ ψ χ
  | ec φ ψ       : Deduction H $ Axioms.ElimContra φ ψ

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩

notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end


structure Hilbert (α : Type*) where
  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)

import Foundation.Modal.Formula
import Foundation.Modal.System.K
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Lukasiewicz

namespace LO.Modal

open System

variable {α : Type*}

section

/-- instance of inference rule -/
structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where
  antecedents : List (Formula α)
  consequence : Formula α
  /--
  Empty antecedent rule can be simply regarded as axiom rule.
  However, union of all these rules including to `Hilbert.rules` would be too complex for implementation and induction,
  so more than one antecedent is required.
  -/
  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp

namespace Hilbert.InferenceRule

abbrev Necessitation (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[φ], □φ, by simp⟩
abbrev Necessitation.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { Necessitation φ | φ }
notation "⟮Nec⟯" => Necessitation.set

abbrev LoebRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ➝ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev LoebRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { LoebRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Loeb⟯" => LoebRule.set

abbrev HenkinRule (φ : Formula α) : InferenceRule α := ⟨[□φ ⭤ φ], φ, by simp⟩
abbrev HenkinRule.set : Set (InferenceRule α) := { HenkinRule φ | φ }
notation "⟮Henkin⟯" => HenkinRule.set

end Hilbert.InferenceRule

end

  axioms : Theory α
  rules : Set (Hilbert.InferenceRule α)

open System

structure Hilbert.InferenceRule (α : Type*) where

  consequence : Formula α

  antecedents_nonempty : antecedents ≠ [] := by simp
